actual_checks: Full exact report, literal prompt, all provenance/source records and full retained mean-square/fixed-moment prior read. The report adds the deep Guth–Maynard theorem and exact exponent-region comparison instead of repeating the earlier elementary moment family.

Guth–Maynard Theorem 1.1 covers all complex |b_n|<=1 and one-separated times in [0,T]. Lower endpoint is reconciled by assigning its coefficient zero and strict prompt values imply the nonstrict theorem threshold. Formula (1.1) classical comparison is matched, retaining fixed polynomial T ranges and honest subpower constants.

Setting T=N^a,V=N^sigma gives g=max(2-2sigma,18/5-4sigma,a+12/5-4sigma) and c=max(2-2sigma,a+min(1-2sigma,4-6sigma)); the better bound has exponent min(g,c). For sigma>3/4, a<=4sigma-2 makes the classical second term no larger than the first, including endpoint. Sigma>=1 has impossible strict threshold in the standard integral-length convention.

At sigma=3/4 the exponents are max(3/5,a-3/5) and max(1/2,a-1/2); improvement begins precisely a>11/10, breakpoint a=6/5, and a=5/4 gives 13/20 versus classical 3/4. Gap 3/20 equals a fixed 3/25 power of T and is not a subpower. The new theorem itself has conjectured order only for sigma>=4/5 and a<=2sigma-2/5, where the classical range is at least as long. No optimality over all methods or full conjecture conclusion is asserted.
